transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-03 UTC 15:00
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Alex Romero (OakTree CTO), Priya Desai (OakTree Lead ML Eng), Samir Khan (OakTree Platform)

Summary (auto):
Quick demo focused on using the model catalog to move from curation to production. Walked through catalog filters, compatibility matrix, running a quick benchmark from the console, and how Redwood Optimize suggests batching/quantization for cost/lower latency tradeoffs. Discussed enterprise concerns (VPC, SOC2, KMS) and next steps for a short Dedicated pilot.

Topics (auto):
- Catalog filtering and picklist creation
- Bench runner and CSV export
- Compatibility matrix mapping to hardware + quantization profiles
- Rolling from picklist to canary and fallback policies
- Security/SSO and audit logs

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account, and Maya who does the SE walkthroughs is here. How's it going Alex?
[00:10] Alex: Good, thanks. We wanted to see the end-to-end from scouting models through the bench to a production rollout. Priya is the one who will be running the internal tests.
[00:18] Priya: Yep, hi. We're mostly doing summarization and some routing for multi-tenant content. Latency's important but so is cost.
[00:25] Maya: Perfect, that's exactly what this flow is designed for. We'll start in the catalog, narrow to open models that match your latency and token budgets, run a bench with your prompt set, and then show the compatibility matrix that maps to GPU families and quant profiles. Then we'll demo how to push to a canary and set a fallback.
[00:40] Samir: Quick check — we need VPC/private deployment options and KMS integration. Also SOC2 details. Is that in scope?
[00:48] Jordan: Yes, we'll cover that near the end. We also have the security pack and SSO docs, we'll send them after.
[00:54] Maya: Alright jumping in, I'm sharing my screen. This is the Redwood Console catalog view. On the left you can filter by model family, license type, architecture, max token length, and perf profile.
[01:12] Maya: I'll set license to "Apache/MIT-like" and filter for models with <200ms cold-start median on A100-class hardware — oops that metric is estimated from our bench corpus so it's a little noisy.
[01:28] Alex: When you say <200ms, is that per-token or end-to-end on our prompt lengths?
[01:34] Maya: Good call. It's median generation per token for the sample sequences in the profile. We also show p95 end-to-end latency for the full prompt in the bench step.
[01:43] [01:45] Speaker 1 (transcription artifact): yeah yeah okay
[01:47] Maya: Here we have a picklist of 6 models. The console adds an initial compatibility score — that's a weighted score combining accuracy heuristics, latency, and quantization friendliness. We can tweak weights.
[02:05] Priya: Can you show the compat matrix? We need to know which ones are stable with int8 quantization.
[02:11] Maya: Sure, opening the compatibility tab. This matrix maps models to hardware families (A100, H100, T4, Bittensor? - transcription hiccup) and also to our quantization profiles: FP16, int8, 4bit. Cells show expected throughput and a qualitative note about accuracy regressions.
[02:31] Maya: Notice model "open-sentinel-3b" has a green int8 cell with a small accuracy note; it tends to do well with per-channel quantization. "liberty-7b" looks yellow for int8 — we recommend per-layer calibration or 4-bit for production.
[02:46] Alex: How much of the compat matrix is empirical vs inferred?
[02:50] Maya: Good question. It's 60% empirical from bench runs in our lab and 40% inferred from model topology heuristics and kernel mapping. We highlight empirical cells so you can filter only models we've bench-run.
[03:03] Jordan: We try to be explicit about that; the catalog shows a bench-run date and the hardware used so you know what's empirical.
[03:10] Priya: Can we upload our prompt set to run here? We have about 300 representative summarization prompts, varied lengths.
[03:17] Maya: Absolutely. In the bench runner you can upload a CSV — we'll run token-level and quality metrics. I'll do a quick demo with a small subset to keep the run short.
[03:27] [03:29] Maya: Uploading now, selecting 20 samples. I'll pick three models from the picklist: "open-sentinel-3b", "liberty-7b", and "garden-4".
[03:38] Maya: Launching bench. You can choose either hosted run or dedicated cluster. For a quick demo I'm using hosted but for your pilot we'd run on the Dedicated setup you requested.
[03:47] Alex: What's the difference in the metrics between hosted and dedicated?
[03:50] Maya: Hosted uses our mixed hardware pool and gives a general performance profile. Dedicated runs on exact hardware in your reserved pool so the latency/throughput numbers are more predictable. The bench report includes both when you select "run on dedicated" and you have Dedicated provisioned.
[04:04] [04:06] System (auto): Bench started — estimated time 7 minutes for 20 samples.
[04:10] Priya: While that runs, can you show Optimize suggestions for batching and cache settings? We're worried about multi-tenant tail latency.
[04:17] Maya: Sure. In Optimize -> Recommendations, we analyze your workload pattern (seq len distribution if uploaded) and produce suggestions like preferred batch size, min and max batch window, and KV cache settings. For summarization we often suggest smaller continuous batching and aggressive prefix caching for repeated doc headers.
[04:34] Maya: Here's a suggestion: batch size 8, batch window 12ms, enable KV prefix caching for doc chunks, and recommend int8 quant profile #3 for open-sentinel-3b to hit your cost target. It also estimates unit token cost and p95 latency.
[04:50] Samir: That batch window seems small, is that tunable at runtime? We have spikes during jobs.
[04:55] Maya: Yes, you can set autoscaling thresholds and burst policies in Dedicated. We also have smart routing so non-critical traffic can be routed to a lower-cost variant during spikes.
[05:06] [05:08] Jordan: Bench results are starting to populate — Maya, you can scroll to results.
[05:12] Maya: Ok results for 20 samples. Summary table shows latency averages, p95, token cost, and a small quality metric (ROUGE-lite proxy from our runner). For open-sentinel-3b: mean latency 120ms, p95 200ms, cost per 1k tokens $0.85 (hosted estimate). Liberty-7b: mean 180ms p95 340ms cost $1.10; Garden-4: 95ms mean, but lower ROUGE-like score on long docs.
[05:43] Priya: Those cost numbers — are they normalized to your hosted pricing? We need to map to Reserved/Dedicated pricing.
[05:49] Jordan: The bench CSV includes a column with Dedicated-adjusted cost given a hypothetical reserved price (we apply a discount factor depending on the committed tier). We'll include that CSV in the export.
[06:00] Maya: I'm exporting the bench report now — you can download raw timings and the picklist recommendation. The console also auto generates a "shortlist" playbook: top 2 candidates with recommended quant profile and rollout strategy.
[06:12] Alex: Show the rollout strategy. We want canary by tenant percentage, not by traffic.
[06:17] Maya: Console supports canary by route, by weighted traffic, or by metadata (tenant). You can pick tenant attribute and we’ll roll 5% of tenants to the new model, monitor quality/regressions via evals, then expand to 25%, 50%, etc. There’s automatic fallback to prior variant if latency or quality regressions exceed thresholds.
[06:34] Priya: How are regressions measured? Are they tied to our prompt set?
[06:38] Maya: Yes, you can pin an eval suite — the same prompt set you upload — and set regression thresholds on metrics (e.g., relative ROUGE drop > 2%). We also track hallucination indicators and fuzzy match metrics.
[06:49] [06:51] Speaker 2 (murmur): okay great
[06:53] Samir: About security — we need audit logs at token-level or just request-level? Compliance requires traceability.
[07:00] Jordan: We provide request-level audit logs, token-level metadata for billing, and optional deeper traces for Private deployments with HSM/KMS integration. For sensitive data we recommend Private (VPC) with customer KMS.
[07:12] Alex: What's the onboarding timeline for Dedicated? We have procurement deadlines end of month.
[07:16] Jordan: Typical Dedicated spin-up is 2–4 weeks depending on reserved capacity and network setup, Private on-premier is longer. For a short pilot we can provision a small Dedicated pool faster if you sign the trial SOW.
[07:28] [07:30] System (auto): Bench finished — exporting results.
[07:32] Maya: Bench complete. I can paste the top-level CSV numbers in chat. Open-sentinel-3b: p95 200ms, quality proxy 0.78. Liberty-7b: p95 340ms, proxy 0.81 but higher cost. Garden-4: p95 95ms quality 0.72. Our picklist recommendation (cost-conscious) ranks open-sentinel-3b first, then liberty-7b.
[07:51] Priya: Interesting — Garden-4 is fastest but drops on quality for longer docs. That aligns with our internal evals.
[07:58] Maya: We can also run a short quant sensitivity sweep — try int8 vs 4-bit to see accuracy delta. Do you want that added to the trial runs?
[08:07] Priya: Yes please, at least for the two top candidates.
[08:11] Jordan: I'll add that to the trial scope.
[08:14] Alex: One more — can Redwood's runtime do on-the-fly model variant fallback per request? e.g., if the int8 inference misses a safety check or hallucination metric, fallback to FP16 variant?
[08:25] Maya: Yes, the smart-routing rules can fallback to a safer variant on per-request signals. You can chain functions so a safety classifier runs first, and if it fails we re-route to a higher-precision variant synchronously or queue for async re-score.
[08:39] Samir: Do you expose metrics for token accounting per-tenant? We need per-team chargebacks.
[08:44] Jordan: Token-level billing with tags is available; Redwood Console shows per-tenant token breakdown and cost attribution. You can also pull reports via API.
[08:55] [09:00] Maya: Okay, wrapping up demo portion — I'll show the generated playbook notes: selected model, quant profile, batch settings, rollout plan, and the suggested monitoring evals. This playbook can be exported as a SRE-runbook for your platform team.
[09:16] Priya: Nice, that would help our ops folks. Could you attach an example runbook in the export?
[09:22] Jordan: Yes, we'll include a sample runbook and the bench CSV.
[09:26] Alex: About procurement — we'll need SSO/SAML docs and SOC2 report. Also list of sub-processors.
[09:33] Jordan: We'll attach the security pack and subprocessors list. Also happy to set up a security call with our compliance lead.
[09:40] Priya: For the trial, can we get a 2-week Dedicated cluster with the three models bench-run and quant sweeps?
[09:46] Jordan: Yes that's the plan. We'll scope it as a pilot: two weeks, small Dedicated pool, bench runs and int8/4-bit sweeps, and a canary rollout by tenant.
[09:56] Samir: Ok timeline: if you send the trial SOW today we can sign and aim to kick off next Monday.
[10:02] Jordan: I'll draft the SOW and pricing sheet and send by Friday.
[10:07] Maya: Action items I've noted — I'll run full bench on Dedicated once you provide the full 300 prompt CSV.
[10:13] Alex: We'll share that and schedule a security call.
[10:17] Jordan: Great. Quick recap of next steps: Jordan to send pricing & SOW, Maya to export bench and run quant sweeps on Dedicated, Priya to share prompt set, OakTree to review security docs and confirm pilot sign-off.
[10:30] Alex: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[10:33] Jordan: Thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.
